line: Lenovo Chromebook Plus 14 OLED (2025, Kompanio Ultra)
config_name: Lenovo Chromebook Plus 14" OLED — MediaTek Kompanio Ultra 910, 16GB RAM, 256GB SSD, 14" FHD OLED touch

specs.cpu: MediaTek Kompanio Ultra 910 (Arm, 8-core big-small with NPU)
specs.storage_type: SSD (soldered; no user upgrade path advertised)
specs.ports: USB4/USB-C x2, USB-A, HDMI, 3.5mm (Kompanio Ultra platform supports USB4)

battery.notes: Kompanio Ultra Arm efficiency + ChromeOS: ~9-11h real web use expected for this class.

price.notes: Regular $1,349.95; sale $1,149.95 (BBY-verified 2026-11-24, SKU 19767599). Only OLED Chromebook stocked at BBY CA.

offers.name: Lenovo Chromebook Plus 14" OLED Touchscreen Chromebook - MediaTek Kompanio Ultra 910 - 16GB LPDDR5x - 256GB SSD - ChromeOS - Seashell

praises: The only OLED Chromebook in Canadian retail — infinite contrast makes web video and dark-mode UI look flagship
16GB RAM is double the Chromebook Plus minimum, so dozens of tabs plus Android apps never swap
Kompanio Ultra 910 is the fastest ChromeOS CPU sold — smooth 4K AV1 playback and snappy Gemini features
Touchscreen plus premium chassis: feels like a $1,600 ultrabook at the sale price
Arm efficiency keeps it silent and cool with battery still around 10 real hours
complaints: $1,150-1,350 for a Chromebook is a hard sell when a $450 Chromebook Plus covers 90% of the use case
Still ChromeOS: the OLED panel cannot run desktop Photoshop/Office — the OS ceiling is the same as the $450 model
OLED touch at 60Hz with no active pen bundled — no stylus story despite the touch layer
16GB/256GB are soldered — no upgrade path at a premium price
FHD (1920x1080) on a premium OLED panel is lower resolution than OLED Windows rivals at this money

standouts: Only OLED + only 16GB Chromebook in the CA inventory — the premium ChromeOS experience, and the Kompanio Ultra 910 is the fastest Chromebook CPU available
dealbreakers: $1,149.95+ buys a far more capable Windows ultrabook for anyone who actually needs desktop apps — this is only worth it as a deliberate ChromeOS purchase
design_philosophy: Lenovo's halo Chromebook: put MediaTek's first flagship Arm chip, 16GB RAM, and an OLED touch panel into the 14" chassis to prove ChromeOS can be premium, not just cheap. It is the anti-thesis of the value tier — the same OS, wrapped in genuinely flagship hardware for buyers who want the simplest possible machine without the usual budget compromises.
